description: MTKClient (latest release, not main): MediaTek reverse engineering and flashing tool. Reads and writes flash over BROM, preloader and DA, unlocks seccfg (bootloader), dumps keys and RPMB.
notes: Latest upstream release, not main: v2.1.4.1 from 18 March 2026. gesu/MTKClient tracks main and has fixes
this release lacks, among them a safer 'da seccfg unlock' (this release's unlock can brick some devices).
Only one of MTKClient and MTKClient-Release can be installed: both add the same commands (mtk, mtk_gui, ...). Installing one while the other is installed stops.
Install needs internet access: uv downloads a private Python 3.14 (x64, also on ARM64, because the bundled
libusb is x64 only) into the app folder, and the packages pinned in upstream's uv.lock from PyPI.
USB driver: Windows binds MediaTek's BROM/preloader port (VID_0E8D, PID_0003 or PID_2000) to a serial driver,
which libusb cannot open. Either bind WinUSB to it with Zadig (suggested gesu/Zadig), or install UsbDk
(suggested gesu/UsbDk): mtkclient falls back to it on 'Access denied' and keeps the serial driver.
'mtk fs' (mount partitions) needs the WinFsp driver: see the suggested nonportable/winfsp-np.
mtkclient writes 'logs' (log.txt and the per-device hwparam keys) into the current folder. The MTKClient shortcut
in Scoop Apps starts the GUI where that folder is persisted; 'mtk' from a console writes into the console's folder.
Writing, erasing and 'da seccfg unlock' change the device and can brick it; unlocking also wipes userdata.
Back up first (mtk rl), and use --critical only if you know your device needs it.
pre_install: # MTKClient adds the same commands (mtk, mtk_gui, ...): only one of the two may be installed.
if ($cmd -eq 'install' -and (installed 'MTKClient')) { error "$app conflicts with MTKClient, which is installed. Run 'scoop uninstall MTKClient' first."; break }

script: # There is no Windows build: uv installs the source from $dir with the dependency versions pinned in
# upstream's uv.lock into a virtual environment in the app folder, on a private Python kept there too, so
# updates of Scoop's own python cannot break it. The Python is x64 also on ARM64 (runs emulated), because
# the libusb-1.0.dll bundled with mtkclient is x64 only and PySide6 has no 32-bit build.
# --no-editable: the console scripts import mtkclient.mtk, which exists only in the built wheel.
if ($LASTEXITCODE) { throw "uv sync failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }
